sentences: Your Django endpoint returns the wrong total, but only while the server is running. Print statements and restarting the server get old fast.
Put a breakpoint in the view that builds the response.
Start Django under the debugger. Pick Django runserver from the list, and that is it. No launch file to write.
Send the request from the editor. The server stops right inside your view, with the request and every local variable in view.
Continue, and the response comes back to the editor, next to the request.
Async code is worse: an exception inside a task can vanish without a trace. So tell the debugger to stop on every exception your code does not handle.
Run the script, and it stops on the exact line that raised, with the value that caused it.
A live request and a lost async error, both caught in the editor, without a single print.

cards.label: Chapter 6 · Debugging Django
cards.title: Catch it while the server runs
cards.problem: A Django view returns the wrong total, and an async task loses its error. Catch both live, in the editor.
cards.before: Write a launch.json for Django, send the request from another tool, and add a print to find the async error.
cards.after: Space d c starts Django under the debugger, Space r r sends the request, Space b e stops on unhandled exceptions.
